motion-quantities-s1.title: A cart timed at four marks
motion-quantities-s1.text: A student times a cart rolling along a level track and records its position at each time.

motion-quantities-s2.title: A cart and a motion detector
motion-quantities-s2.html: Key: the box at the left is the motion detector; the arrow shows the cart's direction of motion.

items.q: What is the cart's average velocity from 0.0 s to 3.0 s?

why.correct: Average velocity is Δx/Δt = (1.40 m − 0.20 m) / 3.0 s = 0.40 m/s.
options: Right: the change in position divided by the time interval.
This divides the final position by the time; it ignores the starting position of 0.20 m.
This is the change in position alone, with no division by the time interval.
This divides the time by the position change instead of position by time.

items.q: What is the cart's displacement from 1.0 s to 3.0 s? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the final position, not the change in position. Subtract where it started.

why.correct: Δx = 1.40 m − 0.60 m = 0.80 m, to two significant figures.

items.q: How does the cart's velocity change over the four readings?

why.correct: The position grows by 0.40 m every second, so the velocity is constant.
options: Right: equal changes in equal times mean constant velocity.
The position changes by the same amount each second, so the velocity is not growing.
Each interval covers the same 0.40 m, so the cart is not slowing.
The position keeps increasing, so the cart never turns around.

items.q: The cart keeps the same motion. Where is it at 5.0 s?

why.correct: It moves 0.40 m each second, so 2.0 s after 1.40 m it is at 1.40 + 0.80 = 2.20 m.
options: Right: two more seconds at 0.40 m/s add 0.80 m.
This multiplies 0.40 m/s by 5.0 s and leaves out the starting position.
This adds only one second of motion after 3.0 s.
This adds 0.40 m for each of the five seconds to 0.40 m, not to the start.

items.q: The detector reports the cart's position increasing. Which sign does its velocity have, with positive to the right?

why.correct: Moving away from the detector to the right means position increases, so the velocity is positive.
options: Right: the sign of velocity is the direction of motion.
Negative would mean the position decreases, toward the detector.
A zero velocity would leave the position unchanged.
The sign depends on the direction, not on how fast the cart moves.

items.q: The cart goes from 0.50 m to 1.70 m in 2.0 s. What is its average velocity, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: that divides the final position by the time; use the change in position.

items.q: The cart speeds up while moving right. What is the direction of its acceleration?

why.correct: Speeding up means the acceleration points the same way as the velocity: right.
options: Right: speeding up puts acceleration along the velocity.
An acceleration to the left would slow a cart moving right.
Nothing in the motion changes vertically.
The track is level and nothing changes vertically.

items.q: The cart's velocity rises from 0.20 m/s to 0.80 m/s in 3.0 s. What is its average acceleration? Give the value and its unit.

why.correct: Displacement has a size and a direction.
options: Distance is the path length, a size only.

items.q: A runner goes 400 m around a track and stops where she started. What is her displacement?

why.correct: She ends where she began, so the change in position is zero.
options: Right: same start and end position.
That is the distance, the path length.
Half the lap is not where she stops.
This doubles the distance for no reason.

items.q: A ball rolls 150 cm in 2.5 s. What is its average speed, in m/s?
Which of these describe an object that is accelerating?
options: It moves at a steady speed in a straight line

why.correct: Acceleration is any change in velocity, in size or direction.
options: Constant speed in a line means constant velocity.
At rest, the velocity stays zero.

items.q: Put the steps for finding an average velocity from two readings in order.
options: Read the starting and final positions
Divide the displacement by the time interval

why.correct: Positions, then their difference, then the time interval, then divide.

items.q: Two carts have the same average velocity over 4.0 s. What must be true?
options: They have the same speed at 2.0 s
They start at the same place

why.correct: Same average velocity over the same time means the same displacement.
options: Right: Δx = v_avg Δt for both.
The paths can differ if one turns around.
An average over 4.0 s says nothing about the speed at one instant.
They can start anywhere and still move the same amount.

items.q: A car goes from 10 m/s to 4 m/s in 2.0 s, moving forward. What is its average acceleration?

why.correct: a = (4 − 10) m/s / 2.0 s = −3.0 m/s²; negative because it slows while moving forward.
options: Right: change in velocity over time, with its sign.
The size is right but the sign: slowing while moving forward is negative.
This uses the average of the speeds, not their change.
This is the change in velocity, not divided by the time.
